# check_list

Lists the checks the tree of rev, main by default, describes in .swarmops/checks.toml (version 1), or else check.argv of .swarmops/workspaces.json as the one check default: each with its argv, its directory, its timeout, the JUnit and SARIF reports it declares and the digest of its definition, sorted by name, with the tree they were read from. Reads only. A tree with neither file lists none; a file that does not read is E\_CHECK\_FILE with its line and key. Nothing runs a check.

```yaml
title: "check_list"
description: "List a tree's checks."
since: "0.1.0"
mutates: false
identity_required: false
cli_command: "swarmops check list"
envelope_op: "check_list"
request_type: "CheckListReq"
annotations: {"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false,"readOnlyHint":true}
max_result_chars: null
```

## Input schema

`arguments` is a `CheckListReq`: `swarmops schema CheckListReq` prints the type. A field the type does not know is ignored.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rev` | string | no | `"main"` | The changeset whose tree's checks to list; `main` when omitted. A revision as the caller wrote it, for the store to resolve: a ref name (`main`, `release/1.2`), a full 64-hex changeset id or a unique prefix of at least 12 hex digits, or a ref's earlier value: `<ref>@{N}` the value it held N moves before its current one (`@{0}` is the current value), `<ref>@{at=<unix seconds>}` the value set by its newest move recorded at or before that instant (the writer's clock, moves read in journal order); optionally followed by `~N` for the N-th first-parent ancestor. |
| `stage` | string or null | no |  | Only the checks of this stage; every check when omitted. |

## Annotations

It only reads the store.

| Annotation | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `destructiveHint` | `false` | True: a tool that changes the store may overwrite or delete what is there, not only add to it. |
| `idempotentHint` | `true` | True: calling it again with the same arguments changes nothing more. |
| `openWorldHint` | `false` | True: it reaches beyond a closed set of things. Every tool here stays inside the store. |
| `readOnlyHint` | `true` | True: the tool does not change its environment, the store. |

Its entry in `tools/list` carries no `_meta`.

## CLI command

[`swarmops check list`](../commands/check-list.md) runs the same operation and prints the same envelope.

## Examples

### MCP

```json
{
  "id": 48,
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "arguments": {},
    "name": "check_list"
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "id": 48,
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "result": {
    "content": [
      {
        "text": "{\"api\":1,\"meta\":{\"auth\":\"trust\",\"elapsed_ms\":\"[elapsed_ms]\",\"repo\":\"[tmp]/store\",\"resolved\":{\"[grouped]\":\"[grouped]\",\"main\":\"[grouped]\"}},\"ok\":true,\"op\":\"check_list\",\"result\":{\"checks\":[],\"tree\":\"[id20]\",\"vouched\":false}}",
        "type": "text"
      }
    ],
    "isError": false,
    "structuredContent": {
      "api": 1,
      "meta": {
        "auth": "trust",
        "elapsed_ms": "[elapsed_ms]",
        "repo": "[tmp]/store",
        "resolved": {
          "[grouped]": "[grouped]",
          "main": "[grouped]"
        }
      },
      "ok": true,
      "op": "check_list",
      "result": {
        "checks": [],
        "tree": "[id20]",
        "vouched": false
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The server ran as `swarmops mcp --repo [tmp]/store --as agent/worker-17`, after `initialize`. Recorded by the MCP tests. A name in square brackets, such as `[tmp]` or `[c1]`, stands for what differs from run to run: the test's temporary directory, an id, a time, the version.

## Details

It reads the tree of `rev` (default `main`) from the store the server was started on: there is no
directory form here, which `swarmops check list --dir` serves on the command line.
An answer from the store says `vouched: false` and names the tree it read; with `stage`, it lists
only the checks of that stage and echoes it. Each check's declared JUnit and SARIF reports come in
its `reports`.
Nothing runs the checks it lists.

## Return information

A tool result: the envelope, whose `op` is `check_list`, as `structuredContent` and again as the text of its one `content` block. `isError` is true exactly when the envelope's `ok` is false. On success the envelope's `result` is what [`swarmops check list`](../commands/check-list.md#return-information) returns.

## Errors

A failed call is a tool result with `isError: true`; the envelope's `error.code` is one of the [error codes](../errors.md).

- [`E_INVALID_ARG`](../errors.md#e_invalid_arg): arguments that do not fit `CheckListReq`, a field named twice among them included, or that break one of the server's own rules.
- [`E_NOT_A_REPO`](../errors.md#e_not_a_repo): the server's store is not there; the server serves on.
- [`E_INTERNAL`](../errors.md#e_internal): the operation panicked, a bug.

Then the errors of the operation, as [`swarmops check list`](../commands/check-list.md#errors) lists them.
